setup: Deep Rock Galactic: Survivor running, library 2026.09.07, build 6266665

probe_run_1.speed: no meaning search, as Speed requires

live_ask_same_session.where: read off Show details on a real Strategy Ask minutes earlier

verdict: The probe PASSES and the real thing does not. That is a fault in the check.
the_finding: The probe reports 23 to 38 milliseconds against a one-second budget and prints PASS. A real Ask on the same device, in the same session, minutes apart, took 1067 milliseconds for the same step and would print OVER BUDGET. So the check as built would report a healthy device while every question a person actually asks is over the line.
why_this_matters: This is the failure the budget was written to prevent, reproduced in the budget's own check. A check that passes while the real thing fails is worse than no check, because it converts an open question into a false all-clear.
what_is_different: The probe searches several times inside one process, so whatever costs the second is already paid by its first call. A real Ask pays it every time. The older device evidence agrees: three separate Asks in a row each took about 1080 to 1230 milliseconds, with no first-one-is-slow shape. So the cost is per Ask, not per search, and the probe never pays it.
not_yet_known: Why an Ask pays it and a probe does not. A reasonable lead, untested: the chat model and the embedding model compete for memory on the Deck, so running a chat inference may evict the embedding model and the next Ask reloads it. That would explain both the per-Ask cost and the creep since August as the chat model grew.
what_the_check_should_do: Measure the step inside a real Ask, or make the probe pay the same cost the first Ask does - a fresh process per reading, or an explicit unload before measuring. Until then the probe's PASS should not be read as the device being within budget.
verdict_for_the_row: FAIL - the check does not measure the thing the budget is about.
